title: Cifral — Proposal chapter catalog
description: The canonical, versioned superset of chapters a Cifral proposal can contain. This is the CLOSED VOCABULARY shared by the Module 2 agents, the render context (modules/proposal/render_context.js) and the .docx template tags — an id that is not in here has no agent that knows how to write it and no template block to render it. Per-client customization does NOT happen in this file: it happens in the client's 'Proposal Config' Google Sheet (docs/CLIENT-DRIVE-SETUP.md), which selects, reorders, renames and supplies text OVER this vocabulary. Same split as pricing: the repo owns the formula, Drive owns the numbers. Every chapter id and section id is also a RENDER KEY: it produces {#has_<id>}, {#<id>.parrafos} and {#<id>.bullets} in the template, exactly like the seven narrative sections did before. Ids must be valid Jexl identifiers — ASCII, lowercase, underscores only, no accents and no '-' (Jexl reads '-' as subtraction).

role.es: Selector de cláusulas (motor de reglas determinista)

content_types.generated: Written by an LLM agent, specific to this project.
content_types.boilerplate: Selected from the client's clause library (Proposal Config sheet, tab 'Content'). Never LLM-written — this is contract text.
content_types.calculated: Derived deterministically from RFQ / pricing data. Never LLM-written.
content_types.mixed: A generated body plus boilerplate clauses merged into the same paragraph stream.

chapters.guidance: Must read standalone: someone who reads only this page knows what is being bought, why, what it costs and when it lands. No jargon, no acronyms without expansion, client's language not ours. Written LAST, from A1+A2 output.
What this offer is built on. Reference documents must be dated and revision-stamped — this is what protects against 'but the spec said'.
Prove we understood the problem before proposing anything. Quantify the pain with the client's own numbers (downtime, obsolescence, spares lead time). Never invent figures the RFQ did not provide.
The engineering argument. Architecture first, then what physically changes, then how it is controlled. Name component categories, never invent brands, part numbers or performance figures.

title.es: Descripción funcional y cambios respecto a la instalación actual
title.en: Functional description and changes to the existing installation

chapters.guidance: DELIVERABLES ONLY — what physically or digitally changes hands. Everything about HOW it gets done belongs in 'ejecucion'. Procurement reads this line by line against the tender, so be enumerable, not narrative.

title.es: Resumen de lo incluido y no incluido
title.en: Summary of what is and is not included

chapters.guidance: SERVICES ONLY — how the deliverables get installed, tested and handed over. Engineering evaluates risk here, so be concrete about sequence, duration and who does what.

title.es: Inspección previa y toma de datos
Plan de pruebas y criterios de aceptación

chapters.guidance: How the project is run and controlled. The schedule lives here even when project management is out of scope — the client always needs to know when things land.

title.es: Calidad y plan de puntos de inspección

chapters.guidance: THE brownfield differentiator. The client's number one fear is 'will you stop my plant'. Answer it explicitly: what keeps running, what the fallback is if a step fails, how the old system stays available until the new one is proven.

title.es: Medio ambiente y gestión de residuos
Condiciones técnicas y requisitos del emplazamiento

chapters.guidance: What the client must provide for the offered price to hold. Numbered obligations, because each one is a change order if unmet.

title.es: Jornadas de trabajo y disponibilidad del sistema

chapters.guidance: The commercial shield, consolidated in ONE place instead of scattered across four. Every assumption and exclusion is numbered so a change order can cite it.

title.es: Condiciones que originan una orden de cambio

chapters.guidance: Never LLM-written. Prices come from Module 3, terms from the client's clause library. A proposal_only request drops this whole chapter.

title.es: Conceptos no incluidos en el precio

chapters.guidance: Contract text, never generated. The recurring-services subsection is the upsell hook — it is the only place in the document that talks about life after handover.

title.es: Soporte técnico y niveles de servicio

chapters.guidance: Pure contract text from the client's clause library. An LLM must never write or paraphrase this chapter.
Tell the reader exactly how to say yes: who to contact, what to send, what happens in the first two weeks after the order. One short page.
Escape hatch: title and body come entirely from the client's Proposal Config sheet. No agent writes it.

annexes.guidance: Requirement -> where it is answered -> complies / deviation. This is what scores points in a public tender and what a human under time pressure skips.

legacy_key_map._comment: Phase-11 render keys -> catalog ids. Old .docx templates must be rebuilt; there is no automatic migration (same as the Google Docs -> docxtemplater move).

column_labels._comment: Header labels for table columns, shared across every table that uses the column. templates/build-templates.js renders these as the header row; docs/TEMPLATE-GUIDE.md documents them.
